Problem: In triangle $ABC$ , side $AB$ has length $10$ , and the $A$ - and $B$ -medians have length $9$ and $12$ , respectively. Compute the area of the triangle.

<reflection>
AB = 10 AM = 9 and BN = 12 With side labels a = BC, b = AC, c = AB = 10, the median formula is m_a = 1/2 sqrt(2b^2 + 2c^2 - a^2)
This assignment is swapped: AM is the median from A to side a, so m_a should be AM = 9, not BN = 12.
Correct the assignments to m_a = AM = 9 and m_b = BN = 12, then use the standard median formulas to set up equations for the side lengths.
</reflection>
